title: Persist test suites and run history across a reload
body:
## Summary
Test suites and their run history live only in React state, so a page reload loses every authored suite.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/TestHarnessPanel/useTestHarnessPanel.ts:19-21 holds suites and suiteRunHistory in useState with no store, database or storage writer. The panel describes authored scenarios as durable work, and the JSON editor invites long edits. Fixed: suites survive a reload through a Zustand persist store or a *-db.ts table, with history capped at the existing 20.

## Flow
- Create a suite and edit scenarios
- Reload the page
- Observe the suite list is empty

## Expected impact
Operators stop re-authoring suites after a reload. A persisted shape needs a version so a later PofTestSpec change cannot crash the panel.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - authored suites survive a reload
Before: 0 persistence writers for suites (useState only)
After: suite list restored after remount in a test
Method: simulation - persistence backend is a design choice this round did not make
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: remount test: create suite, unmount, render again, suite present

title: Allow Ping All while the bridge reads disconnected
body:
## Summary
Ping All is disabled exactly when its failure classification would help most.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/HealthHeader.tsx:69 disables the button on isDisconnected, and src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/index.tsx:49 shows a banner telling the operator to connect first. The probes classify editor-not-running, wrong-port and auth-rejected independently of the store connection status, so a misconfigured port cannot be diagnosed here. Fixed: the button stays enabled and failures carry their kind. Note the acceptance tests pin explicit-click probing, which this keeps.

## Flow
- Enter a wrong port so the store reads disconnected
- Ping All is disabled
- Operator gets no probe classification

## Expected impact
Connection problems get a named cause. Risk: probe traffic to a dead host costs 3 s per route, sequentially.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a disconnected bridge can be diagnosed from this panel
Before: Ping All disabled in 2 of 2 disconnected statuses
After: enabled, and a wrong port reports its ProbeFailureKind
Method: simulation - walked through probes.ts classification, not run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: render with connectionStatus error, click Ping All, assert a data-probe-kind on a row

title: Commit port fields on blur instead of every keystroke
body:
## Summary
Each digit typed in a port field is written to the persisted store as a live port.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/ConnectionSettings.tsx:52 and :78 call setPofPort and setRcPort on change for any value from 1 to 65535, so typing 30040 stores 3, 30, 300 and 3004 in turn. The inputs declare min=1024 while the guard accepts 1, two statements of one rule. Raising the guard to 1024 alone would make the field untypeable, so this needs a draft value committed on blur. Fixed: one rule, applied on commit.

## Flow
- Open connection settings
- Type a new port digit by digit
- Each intermediate port is persisted and clears the readings

## Expected impact
Other consumers of the port stop seeing transient values. Risk: a blur-only commit changes when tests observe the store.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only complete ports reach the store
Before: 4 transient store writes while typing a 5-digit port; min 1024 vs guard 1
After: 1 write on blur; one bound
Method: simulation - counted from the handler, no instrumented run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/ConnectionSettings.tsx:47 min={1024}; :52 v >= 1; same pair at :73 and :78
instrument: fireEvent.change per digit, count setPofPort calls

title: Add a WS port field to the connection settings
body:
## Summary
The panel probes wsPort but offers no way to change it.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/useBridgeEndpointHealth.ts reads wsPort and passes it to probeWsLiveState, and the store exposes setWsPort (src/stores/ue5BridgeStore.ts:48), but src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/ConnectionSettings.tsx renders only host, PoF and Remote Control ports. A failing /pof/live row cannot be corrected here. Fixed: a third port field wired to setWsPort.

## Flow
- Run a WS listener on a non-default port
- /pof/live reports failure
- No field in this panel can correct the port

## Expected impact
The panel can fix all three channels it monitors. Risk: layout of a two-column row.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every probed port is editable where it is probed
Before: 2 of 3 probed ports editable
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - read from the props list
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: render test: change the WS field, assert ue5BridgeStore.wsPort

title: Complete the tab pattern or adopt the shared TabBar
body:
## Summary
The harness tabs declare role=tab without panels or arrow-key movement.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/TestHarnessPanel/index.tsx:66-84 renders role=tablist and role=tab with aria-selected, but no aria-controls, no role=tabpanel and no arrow-key handling, which the role promises. src/components/ui/TabBar is the shared primitive. Fixed: migrate, or implement the full pattern.

## Flow
- Focus a tab with the keyboard
- Press the right arrow
- Focus does not move

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users get the behaviour the role announces. Risk: the shared TabBar is visually different from these tabs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ARIA tab contract holds
Before: 0 tabpanels, 0 aria-controls, 0 arrow handlers
After: 1 tabpanel per tab and arrow-key movement
Method: simulation - grep of index.tsx only
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: render test: ArrowRight moves focus; tabpanel labelled by its tab

title: Make abort cancel the in-flight scenario
body:
## Summary
Clicking abort only stops the next scenario; the running one can hold the suite for up to 120 s.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/TestHarnessPanel/useTestHarnessPanel.ts abortRun sets a ref checked only between scenarios, while src/hooks/useTestRunner.ts:20 polls for up to 120000 ms and exposes no cancel. The button reads "click to abort" throughout. useTestRunner is outside this context, hence not built here. Fixed: runTest exposes an abort that ends its poll.

## Flow
- Run a suite whose first scenario hangs
- Click abort
- The panel stays Running until the poll ends

## Expected impact
Abort means abort. Risk: useTestRunner has three existing test files that pin its lifecycle.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - abort takes effect promptly
Before: up to 120000 ms from click to stop
After: within one poll interval (2000 ms)
Method: simulation - read from the poll loop; useTestRunner is out of scope
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: fake timers: abort during poll, assert runSuite resolves within one interval

title: Remove the unused notIntegrated subsystem flag
body:
## Summary
SubsystemDef.notIntegrated is read in four places and set nowhere.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/types.ts:19 declares the field, and src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/SubsystemGroup.tsx:42-46 and :66 branch on it, but no SUBSYSTEMS entry in src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/constants.ts sets it. A repo-wide grep finds only those readers and no e2e or test use of bridge-group-*-not-integrated. HealthStatus also carries an unknown member that toHealth never assigns. Fixed: remove the flag and its branches.

## Flow
- grep notIntegrated across src and e2e
- Only the type and its readers appear

## Expected impact
Less dead UI to maintain. Risk: a planned not-yet-integrated subsystem would need it back.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dead branches removed
Before: 1 field, 4 read sites, 0 writers
After: 0 of each
Method: probe - grep of src and e2e, removal not applied
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep notIntegrated|not-integrated in src, e2e: only src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/SubsystemGroup.tsx:42,43,46,50,66 and src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/types.ts:19

title: Raise outcome lines in these panels to the 12px floor
body:
## Summary
26 uses of the 10px text-2xs size carry outcome and failure text in this context.

## Description
text-2xs counts under src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth and src/components/modules/project-setup/TestHarnessPanel: SubsystemGroup.tsx 9, AuthorTestPanel.tsx 9, WaitingTestsTab.tsx 4, ConnectionSettings.tsx 2, HealthHeader.tsx 1, SnapshotsTab.tsx 1. Several state a verdict, such as probeKindLabel and the Run + settle outcome line. The repo keeps both a meta size of 10px and a 12px AA floor, so each occurrence has to be classified rather than bulk-migrated.

## Flow
- Open Bridge Endpoints after a failed ping
- Read the failure kind at 10px

## Expected impact
Failure text becomes legible. Risk: dense rows may wrap.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - verdict text meets the legibility floor
Before: 26 text-2xs uses, verdict-bearing ones not separated
After: 0 verdict-bearing uses at 10px
Method: probe - count only, per-occurrence classification not done
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: grep -c text-2xs over both panel folders: 26 total; eslint reports no legibility warning for this size
instrument: a per-occurrence classification against the typography scale

title: Decide whether endpoint health polls on an interval
body:
## Summary
The context map describes a polling monitor, but probing is click-only by pinned design.

## Description
context-map.json describes BridgeEndpointHealth as polling endpoints and rendering latency history. src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/useBridgeEndpointHealth.ts has no timer, and acceptance case 8 in src/__tests__/components/project-setup/bridge-endpoint-health.test.tsx pins that nothing touches the bridge before a click. The sparkline therefore grows only by hand. Either the description changes or an opt-in interval is added, which is a product call.

## Flow
- Open the panel and wait
- No sample is added until Ping All is clicked

## Expected impact
The sparkline either becomes a real trend or the description stops promising one. Risk: background traffic against the editor.

## Evaluation
Claim: direction - is continuous monitoring wanted
Before: 0 timers; latency samples added only by clicks
After: owner decision
Method: simulation - no instrument decides a product direction
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/useBridgeEndpointHealth.ts has no setInterval; test file case 8

title: Reject a blank scenario timeout in the card editor
body:
## Summary
Clearing the Timeout field sends a timeout of 0 to the plugin.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/TestHarnessPanel/ScenarioCard.tsx:83 stores Number(e.target.value), so an empty field becomes 0. The JSON path only requires a finite number. What the plugin does with 0 is not known from this tree, so the safe bound needs checking against the plugin source first.

## Flow
- Expand a scenario
- Clear Timeout
- Run the suite with timeout 0

## Expected impact
A cleared field cannot start a run with no time budget. Risk: choosing a floor the plugin does not share.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a scenario always has a usable timeout
Before: 0 accepted from a blank field
After: blank refused, or a stated floor
Method: simulation - plugin behaviour at 0 not observable without a live editor
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: plugin source read for timeout handling, then a unit test on the field

title: Separate failed-probe latency from the sparkline trend
body:
## Summary
Timed-out probes enter the latency buffer and rescale the trend.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/useBridgeEndpointHealth.ts adds every reading with responseMs, and toHealth sets it on failures too, so one 3000 ms timeout scales a series of 5 ms samples to a flat line at the bottom. src/components/modules/project-setup/BridgeEndpointHealth/LatencySparkline.tsx comments that dropouts should read at a glance, so this may be intended; the finding is whether healthy variation stays visible after a failure.

## Flow
- Ping several times healthy
- Take one timeout
- The healthy samples compress to a flat line

## Expected impact
Trends stay readable after an outage. Risk: hiding dropouts if failures are simply excluded.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - healthy variation visible after a timeout
Before: y-range 5..3000 ms after one timeout
After: healthy range retained and failures marked
Method: simulation - two series walked by hand
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: render the sparkline for both series and compare y spread of healthy samples
